system:
You are shown a snapshot of US macroeconomic and market data as it was known at the end of one month between 2007 and 2026.

Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
Key features: unemployment low (z -2), core CPI high relative to the last 3 years (+1.5, with a 12m change of +1.5), the policy rate near its 3-year average but rising, the dollar strong and rising, and gold weak (-2.5 over 6m, so gold has fallen or been flat after a big run). The 10y yield is low relative to its 3-year average, with a 12m change of -1.5, so yields fell over the year.

Candidate: late 2016 to 2017? Gold fell after the 2016 election, but core CPI wasn't high relative to the prior 3 years then. Another candidate: 2018, where the dollar rose in the spring and summer. The 3-year window for 2018 covers 2015-2018, when the policy rate was rising, so a policy-rate z near 0 with +0.5 is plausible. But the 10y yield in 2018 was rising, not falling.

Other candidate: 2014-2015, with unemployment falling and a strong dollar, but core CPI was low then.

Another candidate: late 2024 to early 2025. The unemployment rate z of -2 relative to 2022-2025 fits, with a low of 3.4-4.2. The policy rate z near 0 and rising 3m doesn't fit, since cuts happened in late 2024. The 10y yield z of -1.5 doesn't fit either.

Another candidate: mid-2019? The dollar was strong, but core CPI wasn't high.

Another candidate: 2023, where the 3-year window includes 2020-2021. The unemployment z would be near 0 or negative, and the policy rate would be high.

Another candidate: 2006-2007 isn't in range. Early 2008? The unemployment rate was rising then.

Another candidate: Dec 2022 to early 2023 (gold fell in H2 2022, and the dollar peaked in Sept-Oct 2022). Then the policy rate z would be high, not +0.

Another candidate: Sept-Oct 2018? Gold fell from April to August 2018, the dollar was up 12m (+1.5) and 3m, the VIX was low, and core CPI was elevated vs 2015-2018. The 10y yield z would be high, though.

Another candidate: mid-2021 to mid-2022? Not consistent.

Another candidate: Jan 2026? Gold has rallied, so no.

Another candidate: mid-2011 to 2012? Gold was high then.

Another candidate: early 2015 to mid-2015: the 3-year window 2012-2015 had core CPI near 1.7%, so it wouldn't be high.

Another candidate: 2010? Unemployment would be high.

Another candidate: 2019 with a 10y z of -1.5. The window 2016-2019 includes the 10y at 1.5-3.2%. In mid-2019 the 10y fell to ~2%, but the 3m change would be negative. In Jan-Feb 2018, the 10y rose.

Another candidate: April-May 2025? Gold was high, so no.

Another candidate: mid-2024? Gold was up, so no.

Another candidate: 2005 isn't in range. I'll settle on 2018, though the 10y doesn't fit. Late 2018 (Nov-Dec): the dollar was up, the 10y z would be high but falling, and equities fell. Equity returns here are mixed and mildly negative. The 10y z of -1.5 with a 12m change of -1.5 fits ... Jan 2024? Not quite.

I'll go with late 2023 to early 2024? Gold was up, so that doesn't fit either.

I'll guess mid-2018 anyway.
